answer: Enforcement-grade identity binding treats each agent's on-chain history as a river of auditable provenance, so a sybil must fabricate consistent prior conduct rather than a fresh keypair. Registration demands a quartz-hard attestation chain linking the agent to a bonded legal entity whose principals bear disclosed liability, forcing attackers to capitalize real entities per identity. That cost deters mass fabrication but fails where saffron-thin shell entities in permissive jurisdictions dilute attribution, so regulators must pierce to beneficial owners.
